office_does: The treasurer is custodian of county funds and banker for local districts: collecting property and other taxes, distributing revenue, investing idle cash, administering debt and overseeing banking.
race_blurb: Shawn Hill, a longtime chief deputy appointed treasurer in July 2025, is seeking his first election against Wes Cormier, a former two-term county commissioner and appraiser. Hill led the primary about 53% to 47%.

candidates.summary: Appointed Grays Harbor County Treasurer since July 2025 after nearly nine years as chief deputy treasurer, running on trust, nonpartisan administration and continuity.
highlights: Chief deputy treasurer from 2016 until his appointment as treasurer in July 2025 [S3][S5]
Wants monthly payment options for taxpayers without escrow and more help with electronic payments [S5]
Calls for healthy reserves and responsible debt management [S5]
Endorsed by former Treasurer Ken Albert, AFSCME Local #275 and the Grays Harbor Democrats [S2]

experience.basis: About a decade inside the treasurer's office as chief deputy and appointed treasurer; runs on continuity, but has not yet won election to the office.

spending.basis: Single explicit statement of fiscal caution: careful stewardship, healthy reserves, responsible debt management, no unnecessary burdens on future generations.

candidates.summary: Former two-term Grays Harbor County commissioner and former senior real estate appraiser, running on budget and levy experience, accessibility and a streamlined office.
highlights: Says he never voted to raise property taxes and led repeal of the county admission tax [S3]
As commissioner, voted against filling positions not in the adopted budget [S6]
Kept a pledge to serve no more than two terms as commissioner [S3]
Wants a streamlined, cost-effective treasurer's department [S5]

experience.basis: Runs on eight years of elected commissioner budget oversight and seven years as an appraiser, though as a challenger new to the treasurer's office.

spending.basis: Record of voting against unbudgeted positions, 'every budget is negotiable', 2020 call to cut state spending with priority-based budgeting, and a 2026 'cost effective' office pledge.

taxes.basis: Says he never voted to raise property taxes and led the admission-tax repeal; in 2020 called any new tax 'a slap in the face'.

reform.basis: Kept a self-imposed two-term limit and in 2020 refused PAC, special-interest and lobbyist money and endorsements; no current-cycle statement.
